offences.quote: Contract cheating can also include the unauthorised use of artificial intelligence systems to generate some or all of a submission subsequently presented as the student’s own work.
Failure to accurately declare use of AI may also constitute academic misconduct.
Using work generated by artificial intelligence systems and submitting it as if it were the student’s own work.
Contract cheating is the commissioning and submission of work as the student’s own where the student has paid or solicited another person to produce the work on the student’s behalf.
Fabrication is the invention, alteration or falsification of data and evidence that contributes towards assessment.
Disguising work in a deliberate attempt to conceal its origins.
Plagiarism is defined as the presentation of another person’s work or ideas as the student’s own, without proper acknowledgement.
any transgression of the University’s examination room rules, as set out in the Regulations for the Preparation and Conduct of Examinations;
Collusion is the unauthorised co-operation between at least two people, normally with the intent to deceive.
being party to an arrangement whereby a person other than the student would fraudulently represent them at an assessment;
is regarded as self-plagiarism and will be treated in the same way as any other form of plagiarism.

liability.quote: Ignorance of this policy cannot be used to excuse infringements.
A student who shows limited intent to meet good academic practice in spite of having had adequate prior teaching, or as a repeat instance, can be deemed to show academic misconduct.
A student in their early stages of HE (level 3 and 4) or without recent experience of HE in the UK may not have gained the knowledge and skills to demonstrate standards of good academic practice.

detection.quote: AI detection tools should not be used as the basis for academic misconduct allegations.
Data from Services designed to detect the use of artificial intelligence in the production of work;
All work that is submitted electronically will be passed through plagiarism detection software.
a high similarity ‘score’ is not acceptable as a standalone justification for allegations of plagiarism

process.quote: OSACC will review and refer cases as appropriate to the Academic Misconduct Panel or delegated Chair of the Academic Misconduct Panel for consideration.
If the Course Leader (or equivalent) decides that there is sufficient evidence that an offence may have been committed, they shall proceed to a formal allegation.
request a written statement in response to the allegation and submission of any evidence they deem appropriate;
or where a student wishes to respond to the allegation in person (or online), a meeting of the Panel will be arranged

process.quote: If the student does not appear at the meeting, the Panel may proceed with the consideration of the allegation in the student’s absence
signpost support available to the student to enable them to respond, which may include support from their course team, student support services and the Students’ Union;
Students may appeal against the verdict of academic misconduct and/or the penalty imposed under the provisions of the Academic Appeals Procedure.
request a reply within ten working days of the date on which the email is sent;

process.quote: Records should be maintained, in line with GDPR requirements, to enable the identification and monitoring of students who have been judged to have demonstrated poor academic practice.

and the student required to withdraw immediately without being awarded a degree or exit award.

outcomes.quote: Where academic misconduct is proven after work has been formally assessed, this may lead to the withdrawal of credit previously ratified by an Assessment Board or withdrawal of a conferred award.

all proven offences of academic misconduct by students on courses leading to professional registration will be considered by the Assessment Board to determine whether further action should be taken under the Fitness to Practise Procedure.

definitions.quote: “Any action by a student which gives or has the potential to give an unfair advantage in an examination or assessment or might assist someone else to gain an unfair advantage, or any activity likely to undermine the integrity essential to scholarship and research.”
Poor academic practice can be defined as poor scholarship resulting from an individual’s lack of knowledge, understanding and practice of the skills required to be academically literate.
Plagiarism is defined as the presentation of another person’s work or ideas as the student’s own, without proper acknowledgement.
Collusion is the unauthorised co-operation between at least two people, normally with the intent to deceive.
Contract cheating is the commissioning and submission of work as the student’s own where the student has paid or solicited another person to produce the work on the student’s behalf.
Fabrication is the invention, alteration or falsification of data and evidence that contributes towards assessment.
Cheating includes any behaviour which the student would reasonably know would interfere with the fair operation of the assessment process and could gain unfair advantage
